findings.consequence: If a pallet jams at the conveyor entry, the condition goes undetected. The conveyor motor continues driving pallets into the obstruction, risking crushing or piercing of EV battery pack enclosures, mechanical conveyor damage, and motor stall.
findings.evidence: Cause-and-effect matrix item CE-ST10-03 requires that if entry eye PE-1002 (X11) remains blocked for more than 5.0 s while conveyor motor M-1001 (Y10) runs, the conveyor stops and a jam alarm is raised. The parameter table defines jam_time as 5.0 s assigned to T10. The lint report notes X11 is declared but never used. In the program, X11 and T10 are never referenced, M190 is never set, and the reset in R2 (RST M190) is dead code.
findings.proposed_fix: Implement jam timing and alarm latching: add a rung with LD Y10, AND X11, OUT T10 K50; add a subsequent rung with LD T10, SET M190; retain R2 (LD X1, RST M190) to allow fault reset PB-0002 to clear M190 once the jam is cleared.
findings.title: Missing Conveyor Jam Detection Logic (Entry Photo-Eye PE-1002 and Timer T10)

findings.consequence: The conveyor motor can restart automatically without operator intervention upon bimetallic cooling or MCC reset, posing an entanglement, crushing, or shearing hazard to personnel inspecting or clearing the stopped conveyor.
findings.evidence: In R1, M191 is driven with an unlatched OUT coil from LDI X13 (MOL-1001 overload healthy). In R3, M191 sets fault summary M199 to stop Y10. If an overload trips and then self-resets after cooling or is manually reset at the MCC, X13 returns to 1, immediately dropping M191 and M199. Because mode selector SS-0003 (X2) is a maintained switch in AUTO, Y10 immediately restarts without requiring PB-0002 (X1) fault reset.
findings.proposed_fix: Latch the overload trip in R1 using SET M191 on LDI X13. In R2, add logic to reset M191 only when reset PB X1 is pressed and X13 is healthy (LD X1, AND X13, RST M191).
findings.title: Unlatched Motor Overload Alarm Permitting Unexpected Automatic Restart

findings.consequence: An actuator can energize or stay energized during an active E-stop condition. In manual mode or when no pallet is at the stop, spurious release pulses drop the stopper, creating pinch hazards or allowing incoming pallets to blow past ST10 without testing. If release fires while the conveyor motor is stopped, the pallet fails to clear before the stopper rises, deadlocking the transfer.
findings.evidence: R6 fires SET Y11 solely on LDP X14 (pallet release request RQ-1005). There are no interlocks verifying E-stop healthy (X0), auto mode (X2), pallet at stop (M100/X10), or absence of station faults (M199). Furthermore, R8 only resets Y11 when timer T11 completes. If an E-stop occurs while Y11 is ON, Y11 remains energized in PLC memory until T11 finishes. If X14 pulses during E-stop or manual mode, Y11 actuates.
findings.proposed_fix: Interlock R6 with safety and operational conditions: LDP X14, AND X0, AND X2, AND M100, ANI M199, SET Y11. Add an immediate reset condition for Y11 when E-stop is lost or auto mode is exited (LDI X0, ORI X2, OR M199, RST Y11).
findings.title: Missing Interlocks on Stopper Release Solenoid XY-1004

findings.consequence: Resetting the safety relay immediately restarts the conveyor motor, creating an unexpected machinery restart hazard for personnel working near the conveyor who expect motion to remain inhibited until commanded.
findings.evidence: In R3, ORI X0 activates M199 when E-stop healthy contact X0 is lost (X0 = 0). When the E-stop button is pulled out and the hard-wired safety relay is reset, X0 returns to 1, causing M199 to turn OFF immediately. Because SS-0003 (X2) is a maintained AUTO selector, R4 immediately re-energizes Y10 without requiring a fault reset (X1) or explicit start command.
findings.proposed_fix: Implement a latched safety stop bit that sets upon loss of X0 (LDI X0, SET M192). In R2, require fault reset PB X1 to clear M192 only once X0 is healthy (LD X1, AND X0, RST M192). Interlock R4 with ANI M192 to prevent uncommanded restarts upon E-stop safety relay re-engagement.
findings.title: Conveyor Motor Automatic Restart Upon E-Stop Circuit Reset

data.summary: The ST10 conveyor logic exhibits four significant defects: (1) CE-ST10-03 jam detection is entirely missing, leaving entry photo-eye PE-1002 (X11) and timer T10 unused while leaving M190 as dead code; (2) motor overload alarm M191 is unlatched in R1, permitting uncommanded automatic conveyor restart when the overload cools; (3) stopper release solenoid Y11 in R6-R8 lacks E-stop, auto mode, fault, and pallet presence interlocks, permitting actuator motion during E-stop or station stoppage; and (4) conveyor motor Y10 restarts automatically upon E-stop safety relay re-arming without requiring a fault reset.
